problems.title: A perpendicular line sharing an intercept
problems.question: A line passes through C=(2,4),D=(1,5). Find its perpendicular through the same x-intercept.
problems.idea: Find the original line first.
steps: The line is y=-x+6, so its x-intercept is (6,0).
The perpendicular slope is 1. Through (6,0), its equation is y=x-6.

problems.title: Parallel but distinct graphs
problems.question: For which a do y=a+1-3ax and y=(a+8)x+a² have no common point?
problems.idea: Their slopes must agree but intercepts differ.
steps: The intercepts then are -1 and 4, so the lines are distinct and parallel.

problems.title: A coordinate relationship on a line
problems.question: On y=2x-35, find the coordinate sum of the point whose x-coordinate is three times its y-coordinate.
problems.idea: Substitute x=3y.

problems.title: Mixed-number product
problems.question: Evaluate (11/18-1 7/12)(2 1/6+7/30).
problems.idea: Convert the mixed numbers to fractions.

problems.title: Reduce to the requested modulus
problems.question: A≡3,B≡5 modulo 8. Find AB modulo 4.
problems.idea: A remainder modulo 8 also determines the remainder modulo 4.

problems.title: Cancel powers before solving
problems.question: Solve [(-7x)¹¹(49x)²·7]/[(-7x²)³(343x)⁴]=56.
problems.idea: Collect all powers of 7 and x, keeping x≠0.
steps: The two negative factors cancel their signs, leaving 7x³=56.
Thus x³=8 and x=2, which is in the original domain.

problems.title: Undo a shifted argument
problems.question: If g(x-2)=2x+5, find g(x).
problems.idea: Use t=x-2.

problems.title: Cube sum from a sum and a square sum
problems.question: a²+b²=89 and a+b=3. Find a³+b³.
problems.idea: Recover ab, then use the cubic identity.

problems.title: A second meeting after both turn around
problems.question: Travellers start at opposite ends A,B, meet after 2 hours at distances 8 km from A and 6 km from B, then continue and immediately turn at the endpoints. Where is their next meeting?
problems.idea: The speeds are 4 and 3 km/h on a 14 km route.
formulas: After both turn, positions from A are x₁=28-4t and x₂=3t-14.
steps: The first traveller reaches B at t=3.5 h and the second reaches A at t=14/3 h. They do not meet between those turnaround times.
After both turn, equality gives 28-4t=3t-14, so t=6.
Their position is 28-24=4 km from A.

problems.title: Complete the square after a linear constraint
problems.question: Minimize 11x²+4xy+y²-4y+1 subject to x-y=2.
problems.idea: Substitute x=y+2.
steps: The square term is at least zero.
It vanishes at y=-3/2,x=1/2, satisfying the constraint.

problems.title: Successive percentage changes multiply
problems.question: An athlete loses 8% mass, then gains 10% of the new mass. Find the total percentage change.
problems.idea: Use multipliers 0.92 and 1.10.
steps: The final mass is 101.2% of the original.

problems.title: Factor a quartic by grouping
problems.question: Find the sum of real roots of x⁴+x³-8x-8=0.
problems.idea: Group the terms into a common factor x+1.
steps: The final quadratic has discriminant 4-16=-12 and no real roots.
The real roots are -1 and 2, with sum 1.

problems.title: Trailing zeros of a factorial
problems.question: How many zeros end 1·2·…·2001?
problems.idea: Factors of 5 limit the number of factors 10.

problems.title: A product of integer factors equals 3
problems.question: For positive natural x,y, x²+xy-2y²-x+y=3. Find the sum of the solution’s coordinates.
problems.idea: Factor the left side.
steps: Since x,y≥1, the second factor is positive. The positive factor pairs of 3 are (1,3),(3,1).
The other pair would require y=-2/3, not natural.

problems.title: Keep only the integer solution of an absolute-value system
problems.question: 2x+y=5, |2x+3y|=7. Find the product of the coordinates of its integer solution.
problems.idea: Use y=5-2x and both signs.
steps: The -7 case gives x=11/2,y=-6, which is not an integer pair.

problems.title: A tangent-parallel chord makes a 30-degree angle
problems.question: Tangents at circle points A,C meet at B with ABC=120°. D lies on the circle and AD∥BC. The altitude of ACD to AD is 1 cm. Find DC.
problems.idea: The tangent triangle ABC has equal sides BA=BC.
steps: Parallelism gives CAD=30°. The tangent-chord theorem gives ADC=30° as well.
Thus the altitude from C to AD equals DCsin30°=DC/2.

problems.title: Four arcs from three crossing angles
problems.question: In cyclic ABCD, diagonals meet at M with AMB=80°. Lines AB,CD meet at K with AKD=20°, and BC,DA at N with ANB=40°. Find the largest quadrilateral angle.
problems.idea: Use arc sums and absolute differences.
formulas: Let consecutive arcs AB,BC,CD,DA be a,b,c,d. Then a+c=160°, b+d=200°, |b-d|=40°, |a-c|=80°.
steps: Each quadrilateral angle is half a sum of one arc from each pair. The largest intercepted sum is 120°+120°=240°.

problems.title: Contact points of three tangent circles
problems.question: Three circles touch externally in pairs, with centres A,B,C and ABC=90°. Their contact on AC is P; the other contacts are K,M. Find KPM.
problems.idea: Use equal radii to form two isosceles triangles.
steps: In triangle AKP, APK=90°-A/2. In triangle CPM, CPM=90°-C/2.
The rays PA and PC are opposite, so KPM is the remaining part of their straight angle.

problems.title: Adjacent tangent radii cancel
problems.question: Circle centres A,B,C,D form a quadrilateral; circles at adjacent vertices touch externally. Three consecutive side lengths are 2,3,5 cm. Find the fourth.
problems.idea: Each centre distance is the sum of two radii.
steps: Opposite side sums are equal: AB+CD=BC+DA.

problems.title: Nested segment ratios
problems.question: B divides AC with AB:BC=2:1. D divides AB with AD:DB=3:2. Find AD:DC.
problems.idea: Express AD as a fraction of AC.
steps: The remainder DC is 3/5 of AC.

problems.title: A bisector between parallel lines
problems.question: A transversal meets parallel lines at A,B. A bisector at B meets the line through A at C. If AB=1 cm, find AC.
problems.idea: Parallelism transfers one bisected angle to C.
formulas: ABC=ACB by the angle-bisector condition and alternate interior angles.
steps: Triangle ABC has equal angles at B,C.
Their opposite sides AC,AB are equal.

problems.title: Two angles at a bisector foot
problems.question: BK bisects B and AKB:CKB=4:5. Find A-C.
problems.idea: The two angles at K sum to 180°.

problems.title: A perpendicular at the hypotenuse midpoint
problems.question: A right triangle has acute angle 30°. The perpendicular to its hypotenuse at the midpoint meets a leg in a segment of length 2 cm. Find the larger leg.
problems.idea: The intersection on a leg segment is on the longer leg.
formulas: In right triangle AMK, A=30°,MK=2, AM is half the original hypotenuse.

problems.title: Locus of parallel-chord midpoints
problems.question: Describe the set of midpoints of all circle chords parallel to one fixed line.
problems.idea: Each midpoint lies on the perpendicular diameter.
formulas: The perpendicular from a circle centre bisects a chord.
steps: Every interior point of that diameter is the midpoint of one parallel chord.
The endpoints would correspond to zero-length tangent contacts, not genuine chords.
problems.answer: The perpendicular diameter segment without its two endpoints.

problems.title: A leg-diameter circle finds the altitude foot
problems.question: A circle with a right triangle leg as diameter divides the hypotenuse in ratio 3:1. Find the least triangle angle.
problems.idea: The other circle intersection is the foot of the altitude from the right vertex.
formulas: An angle subtending a diameter is right; altitude theorem gives leg-square ratio=split-hypotenuse ratio.
steps: The squared legs have ratio 3:1 or 1:3, so their lengths have ratio √3:1.
